observations: Photo 0: a yellow-painted diesel engine block mounted in what looks like a workshop/skid frame, with fuel filter housing, hoses, wiring loom and a watermark reading 'DNL EQUIPMENT SALES AND ...'.
Photo 1: close-up of a rocker/valve cover with an embossed or stamped identification plate; the text on the plate is too small and blurred to read a model number.
No full side/front view of the engine block, no oil pan, no flywheel housing or ECU shown.
No video, sound, or gauge readout showing the engine running.
No hour-meter or mileage display visible anywhere.
Same dealer watermark appears on both photos, suggesting a stock/dealer photo rather than a photo taken specifically of this unit for the buyer.

identity.kind: large industrial diesel engine, sold as a complete unit for parts

claims.evidence: Photo 1 shows an ID plate on the valve cover but the text is not legible enough to confirm 'C9' or any other model code.
No import paperwork, shipping label, or country-of-origin marking visible in either photo.

claims.claim: Tested and working, no knock, low mileage
claims.evidence: No start-up video, sound clip, compression test, or hour-meter photo provided; the listing itself labels the item '(parts)', which conflicts with a 'working' claim.
No close-up of bolt seals, paint overspray lines, or untouched gasket surfaces to confirm the engine has not been disassembled.

risks.risk: Exact engine model cannot be confirmed (C9 vs other Caterpillar industrial engines of similar yellow livery), and price varies greatly by model.
risks.proof: A clear, well-lit close-up photo of the engine's data/ID plate (serial and model stamp) readable without zoom artifacts.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced at all without this; treat as unidentified Caterpillar industrial engine

risks.risk: Engine may not actually run despite the 'tested and working' claim, especially since it is listed '(parts)'.
risks.proof: A video clip of the engine starting and idling, or a recent compression/leak-down test report.

risks.risk: Completeness of ancillaries (turbo, injectors, ECU/wiring harness, starter, alternator) is unclear from the two photos shown.
risks.proof: Full walk-around photos of all sides of the engine plus close-ups of turbo, injectors, and harness connectors.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a bare long-block, missing ancillaries

risks.risk: Claimed Belgian tokunbo origin and low mileage cannot be checked remotely.
risks.proof: Photo of an hour-meter/odometer-equivalent gauge, or import/customs documentation.
risks.if_unproven: mileage/hours treated as unknown, not low

proof_requests: Clear, in-focus photo of the engine's serial/model ID plate (the one shown in photo 1, taken straight-on and well lit).
Video of the engine starting and running, with audible sound.
Full exterior photos from front, rear, both sides, and top showing turbo, injectors, ECU, and wiring harness.
Photo of any hour-meter, or documentation proving the stated Belgian origin and import history.
response.reason: The photos do not show a legible model plate, so even a worst-case price cannot be set among the very different Caterpillar/industrial engine comparables listed; the running condition and completeness are also unproven.
